--- title: "{{< fa cloud >}} Getting Started with Colab" jupyter: python3 --- Google Colab runs Python in your browser. There is nothing to install, nothing to configure, and it works the same on a Mac, a PC, or a Chromebook. ## Sign in Go to [colab.research.google.com](https://colab.research.google.com) and sign in with your **WFU Google account** (`yourname@wfu.edu`), not a personal Gmail. Wake Forest is a Google Workspace for Education school, so your account already exists. Click **New notebook**. You now have a Python environment. ## Your first cell A notebook is a stack of cells. Click a cell, type, and press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}} to run it. ::: {#0e06c173 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} 2 + 2 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 4 ``` ::: ::: The output appears underneath. Press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}} again and the next cell runs. ## Loading course data Every data set we use lives on this website. You read it straight off the web, so there is no downloading and no file paths to get wrong. ::: {#923e4a6f .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd DATA = "https://lucymcgowan.github.io/sta-363-f26/data/" Auto = pd.read_csv(DATA + "Auto.csv") Auto.head() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
name mpg cylinders displacement horsepower weight acceleration year origin
0 chevrolet chevelle malibu 18.0 8 307.0 130 3504 12.0 70 1
1 buick skylark 320 15.0 8 350.0 165 3693 11.5 70 1
2 plymouth satellite 18.0 8 318.0 150 3436 11.0 70 1
3 amc rebel sst 16.0 8 304.0 150 3433 12.0 70 1
4 ford torino 17.0 8 302.0 140 3449 10.5 70 1
``` ::: ::: That `DATA` line appears at the top of every exercise. Copy it once and change only the file name. The full list is on the [Course Data](data.qmd) page. ## What is already installed Colab comes with everything we need through early November: | Package | What we use it for | |---|---| | `pandas` | data frames | | `numpy` | arrays and simulation | | `matplotlib` | figures | | `scikit-learn` | every model until Thanksgiving | | `torch` | neural networks, already installed | You do not need to install any of these. You do not need the `ISLP` package either, because the data is on this site. ## The one install, in November Starting Friday November 13 we fit neural networks. PyTorch itself is already on Colab, but three helper packages are not. Put this cell at the top of the notebook and run it once per session: ::: {#b61a55d4 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} %pip install -q pytorch-lightning torchinfo torchmetrics ``` ::: It takes a few seconds and does not require a runtime restart. ## Turning on the GPU For the convolutional network days, a GPU makes training minutes faster. Go to **Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Change runtime type** and pick a **GPU** accelerator. Check that it worked: ::: {#901dd316 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} import torch torch.cuda.is_available() ``` ::: `True` means you have one. `False` means Colab did not allocate one right now, which happens on the free tier. Everything we do still runs without a GPU, just more slowly. ## Saving your work A Colab notebook you open from a link is read only until you save your own copy. **File** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Save a copy in Drive** Do this at the start of every class. Your copy lives in a Colab Notebooks folder in your WFU Google Drive and saves automatically after that. ## Things that will surprise you **The runtime disconnects.** If you leave a notebook idle, Colab reclaims it. Your code is safe, but your variables are gone. Fix it by running your cells again from the top. This is why every exercise is short. **Cells remember what you ran, not what is on screen.** If you delete a cell that defined `X`, `X` still exists until the runtime restarts. When something stops making sense, use **Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Restart session and run all**. **Order matters, not position.** Running cells out of order is legal and is the usual cause of confusing errors. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd). ## Working locally instead Install [Miniconda](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html), then: ```bash conda create --name sta363 python=3.12 conda activate sta363 pip install numpy pandas matplotlib scikit-learn statsmodels jupyter ``` Everything on this site works the same way locally. I can help with Colab problems in class; local installation problems are better suited to office hours.
